findings.claim: The seam's stated tier-1 warrant is recorded as an addressee shift, but the couplet and the verse closing the preceding unit carry no addressee at all - the shift is a participant/topic shift, and the signal key overstates it.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.14.1 and oshb:Isa.14.2 are third person throughout at byte tier: יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב and וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ and וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.14.2, byte tier) - no second-person form and no vocative anywhere in the two verses, and oshb:Isa.13.22 closing the preceding unit is likewise third person. The rationale nevertheless says the shift brings a fresh addressee in as the object of both verbs (a verbal object is not an addressee), and observed_substrate_signals records oracle_frame.addressee_shift_restoration_promise. The ruled tier-1 inventory names addressee/scene shifts, vocatives and imperative onsets; the first actual addressee in this stretch is the second-person cluster one verse later at oshb:Isa.14.3 - וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ with מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ and verse-final אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (all oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) - which sits at the NEXT row's opening seam, not at this one. The row's own opening word is the backward-binding כִּי֩ (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), which the rationale itself concedes is syntactically dependent on the preceding unit.
findings.proposed_change: Re-label the driver as a participant/topic shift, or argue it explicitly under the ruled scene-shift class, and replace oracle_frame.addressee_shift_restoration_promise with a key that does not claim an addressee; re-test the medium confidence against the weaker warrant. No span change proposed - the Isa.13.22|Isa.14.1 seam survives on the topic break plus the single-witness setumah recorded at Isa.14.2.

findings.claim: The row records a parashah.* key in observed_substrate_signals; the audit brief bars parashah.* there while the owner-ruled strategy's ratified oss taxonomy lists parashah.* as a permitted key - recorded as a contract conflict for adjudication, not adjudicated here.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries parashah.setumah_tier3_corroboration. The underlying mark claim is sound: the inventory records Isa.14.2 = SAMEKH, the row types it as a setumah (never conflated with petuchah), discloses it single-witness, and marks it non-driving in boundary_evidence_refs; the marks validator passes on all eight rows of this slice. Within this slice the same key class stands in P04-003, P04-004, P04-005, P04-006, P04-010, P04-011 and P05-009 - seven of eight rows - so the conflict is a slice-wide class, recorded once here rather than repeated per row.

findings.claim: The warrant binding the row's opening verse to the next one - and so placing the left edge at Isa.14.3 rather than Isa.14.4 - is a WEB sentence/punctuation fact, the exact tier-4 class barred as driver or corroboration.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale states that the temporal clause at web:Isa.14.3 runs as one sentence into the frame verb at web:Isa.14.4. That one-sentence relation is a property of the WEB rendering alone - web:Isa.14.3 ends on a comma and the next verse opens with a subordinating conjunction in the WEB text - i.e. tier-4 metadata, never boundary evidence and never corroboration. The byte-tier fact that would carry the same continuity is never named: oshb:Isa.14.3 opens וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (byte tier) and oshb:Isa.14.4 continues with the waw-consecutive perfect וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ (byte tier), the protasis-apodosis chain that makes the two verses one syntactic unit under the campaign's continuous-sentence rule. The row's only Hebrew splice is taken from oshb:Isa.14.4, the span's second verse. This is the only tier-4 vocabulary in any of the eight rows of this slice.
findings.proposed_change: Re-ground the continuity clause on the oshb:Isa.14.3|oshb:Isa.14.4 waw-consecutive chain (וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ ... וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ, byte tier) and drop the WEB sentence fact from the warrant. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The ruled tier-1 signal the row relies on at its opening verse - the turn into direct second-person address at Isa.14.3 - is asserted only from the English; that verse's own bytes are neither spliced nor listed in boundary_evidence_refs, while the row ships confidence high.
findings.grounds: device_notes names the shift into direct second-person address at Isa.14.3 and observed_substrate_signals records narrative_frame.direct_second_person_taunt, but boundary_evidence_refs holds web:Isa.14.3, web:Isa.14.4, oshb:Isa.14.4, web:Isa.14.21, web:Isa.14.22 and the oshb:Isa.14.2 setumah entry - there is no oshb:Isa.14.3 anywhere in the row. The signal does stand in that verse's bytes: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) closes on a second-person pronominal, מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) carries two more, and the verse ends אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier). The seam is therefore sound on re-derivation, but as cited the left edge rests on a tier-4 sentence fact plus a tier-3 single-witness setumah, with the tier-1 ground unengaged - which the high confidence does not survive as written.
findings.proposed_change: Add oshb:Isa.14.3 to boundary_evidence_refs and splice its second-person cluster (וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ / מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ / אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ, byte tier) into the rationale as the opening seam's tier-1 ground; re-test the high confidence once the warrant is byte-grounded. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative turns on an exclusivity claim about the eighteen verses of the taunt that carries no digit-bearing sweep citation naming its count object.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative argues that the three-token signature chain is a distinct speech-frame device not used inside the taunt itself - a negative-existence claim over Isa.14.4-Isa.14.21 stated without the sanctioned sweep shorthand and without naming the swept object. Re-swept here the claim holds: the neum skeleton stands in 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys) and its only chapter-14 sites are oshb:Isa.14.22 and oshb:Isa.14.23, none inside Isa.14.4-Isa.14.21. The row's three-token count is likewise byte-confirmed against the source: נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת mid-verse and נְאֻם יְהוָֽה verse-final at oshb:Isa.14.22 (byte tier, the second with no hosts-title, as the row states), and נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת verse-final at oshb:Isa.14.23 (byte tier). No other defect found in this row: the marks are correctly typed (inventory Isa.14.23 = PE, disclosed single-witness and subordinated to the byte-carried chain), the WEB runs are verbatim, and the high confidence survives its evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Append a count-object-naming sweep citation to the exclusivity clause, e.g. a parenthetical recording 23 verses book-wide at skeleton tier for the neum token with the chapter-14 sites exactly Isa.14.22 and Isa.14.23. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: device_notes assigns a two-sided structural bracketing function to a pair of single-witness parashah marks without the tier-3 / non-driving qualifier in the prose that states the function, and the closing mark carries that qualifier nowhere in the row.
findings.grounds: device_notes states that a single-witness petuchah precedes at Isa.14.23 and a single-witness petuchah also closes the unit at Isa.14.27, bracketing the oath-oracle on both sides. Both marks are real and correctly typed against the inventory (Isa.14.23 = PE, Isa.14.27 = PE; petuchah never conflated with setumah) and the marks validator passes, but bracketing on both sides is a structural-function claim made from a layer that is tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets and never a boundary driver. The qualifier appears only on the boundary_evidence_refs entry for oshb:Isa.14.23; the Isa.14.27 petuchah appears in no ref and its prose mention carries single-witness alone. The rationale itself never mentions either mark, so no field states what the marks corroborate - which is in fact byte-carried and sound: the verse-initial oath formula נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.14.24, byte tier).
findings.proposed_change: Carry the tier-3, single-witness, non-driving qualifier into the device_notes sentence and onto the Isa.14.27 petuchah, and name the Isa.14.24 oath formula as the driver the marks corroborate. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The row's left edge depends on reading the mid-verse burden-word at Isa.14.28 as pointing forward, and that directional claim is asserted flatly, with no byte ground and no disclosure of the standing backward-pointing construal that would place Isa.14.28 with the preceding oracle.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale states that the burden-word sits mid-verse as a header reference inside the regnal dating frame, pointing forward to the burden this row's own span carries. The verse's own bytes end הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier) - an anaphoric-capable demonstrative that the row never engages - and nothing else in the verse fixes direction. strongest_rejected_alternative disposes only of the FORM question (mid-verse header reference vs the verse-initial header class), not the direction question, although the second-sentence slot reserved for a mandated rival disclosure is unused. The claim is load-bearing: on the backward construal Isa.14.28 closes the preceding unit and this row opens at Isa.14.29. The forward reading is well supported on other grounds the row does hold (inventory petuchah at Isa.14.27; the Philistia address opening at Isa.14.29), so the boundary is not shown wrong here - the warrant is.
findings.proposed_change: Add the mandated rival-disclosure sentence to strongest_rejected_alternative, naming the backward-pointing construal of the Isa.14.28 dating notice and the byte ground on which it is set aside. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The header-class comparison argues from a verse outside the row's span without mirroring it, and states the massa-header digit without a count-object-naming sweep citation, in the one hazard class the toolkit flags by name.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale contrasts the Isa.14.28 mid-verse burden-word with the verse-initial Babylon and Moab headers. The Moab header is mirrored (web:Isa.15.1 stands in boundary_evidence_refs); the Babylon header, which is at Isa.13.1 and is argued here by name rather than by number, is not - the refs-mirror check cannot catch a verse named without its number, and it passes on this row for that reason. strongest_rejected_alternative separately states the ten verse-initial massa headers without the sanctioned sweep shorthand naming the swept object and unit, in the class where header-massa, the Isa.14.28 header reference and the burden-noun sites must never be blended. The digit is correct and the row's three-way role split is right; only the citation form is short.
findings.proposed_change: Add web:Isa.13.1 to boundary_evidence_refs and give the header digit a count-object-naming sweep citation. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: device_notes states a two-sided bracket function for the parashah marks, and the closing setumah at Isa.14.32 carries no tier or non-driving disclosure anywhere in the row.
findings.grounds: device_notes states that a single-witness petuchah precedes at Isa.14.27 and a single-witness setumah closes the unit at Isa.14.32, bracketing the dated burden. Both marks are real and correctly typed against the inventory (Isa.14.27 = PE, Isa.14.32 = SAMEKH; petuchah never conflated with setumah) and the marks validator passes. boundary_evidence_refs qualifies only oshb:Isa.14.27 as petuchah, single-witness, tier-3, non-driving; the Isa.14.32 setumah stands in no ref and its prose mention carries single-witness alone while the same sentence assigns it a bracketing function.
findings.proposed_change: Qualify the Isa.14.32 setumah as tier-3, single-witness and non-driving at the point where its function is stated. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: device_notes justifies its mark-orientation reading by appeal to practice elsewhere in this stretch - a positional cross-row reference with no verse anchor.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads that the after-the-verse orientation is consistent with the reading used elsewhere in this stretch. The register rule bars positional row references and file-order talk from row prose in every field and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored; this one names no verse. The orientation itself is right and independently checkable without the cross-reference: the inventory carries chapter-final marks (Isa.14.32 is the last verse of its chapter and Isa.20.6 the last verse of its own), which are coherent only as after-the-verse breaks.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the appeal to neighbouring practice with a verse-anchored statement of the orientation. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals records the parashah layer as corroboration, but the only mark in scope is interior to the span and stands at the interior cut the row rejects, not at either of the row's own seams.
findings.grounds: The row's seams are Isa.16.5|Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.12|Isa.16.13; the inventory records no mark at Isa.16.5 or Isa.16.12. The one mark in scope is Isa.16.6 = SAMEKH, which on the after-the-verse orientation the row itself adopts falls at Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7 - inside the span, beside the backward-binding לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.16.7, byte tier) opening the next verse and the second-person plural תֶּהְגּ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.16.7, byte tier), the first addressee to stand since the throne promise. The row handles all of this honestly - the interior orientation and the non-driving tier-3 status are disclosed in both strongest_rejected_alternative and the boundary_evidence_refs qualifier - so the defect is confined to the signal key, which in a field dependent on the row's drivers labels as corroboration a mark that corroborates neither seam. The opening driver itself is byte-carried: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ (oshb:Isa.16.6, byte tier).
findings.proposed_change: Rename the key so it does not claim corroboration of this row's own seams. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The boundary rationale closes on a workflow reference to the authoring part the row sits in.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale ends by saying the unit closes both the chapter and this writer part. The register purge bars file-order talk and administrative references from row prose in every field; this writer part names the authoring artifact rather than the text, and the chapter close is a tier-4 division fact. Neither does evidentiary work - the row's close is carried by the dated divine word at oshb:Isa.16.14 and the single-witness setumah the inventory records there (Isa.16.14 = SAMEKH).
findings.proposed_change: Delete the writer-part reference, and the chapter-close clause with it. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: A closure-named signal key is recorded for a device that stands in the row's opening verse rather than its closing verse.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries oracle_frame.retrospective_closing_colophon. The colophon it names stands at Isa.16.13, the row's first verse; the row's closing verse is Isa.16.14, whose device the row separately and correctly records as speech_formula.but_now_yhwh_has_spoken. Under the oss discipline a closure key is valid only where its device stands in the row's own closing verse. The colophon claim itself is byte-sound - the whole of oshb:Isa.16.13 is spliced at byte tier in the rationale - and the second key is correctly placed.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the key so it does not assert closure at this row's own close, or attach the closure claim to the Isa.16.14 device. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The row ships medium_low confidence on an unresolved question it names, yet records frontier_flag_considered false, out of line with every other low-band row in the same stretch.
findings.grounds: confidence is medium_low and device_notes names a redactional-layering question the row deliberately holds open - genuine evidentiary uncertainty, not the whole-chapter shape cap, since the span is two verses of a fourteen-verse chapter. frontier_flag_considered is nevertheless false. The neighbouring low-band rows, whose medium_low comes from the whole-chapter cap rather than any evidentiary problem, both set it true (Isa.15.1-Isa.15.9 and Isa.20.1-Isa.20.6), as does the low-confidence Isa.21.1-Isa.21.10 row. The campaign requires a frontier-queue row for every low-band chunk, so the one row in this stretch with real held uncertainty is the one not flagged.
findings.proposed_change: Set frontier_flag_considered true and register the held question in the frontier queue. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The sole warrant against dividing the chapter is an exclusivity claim that no fresh time-frame or scene turn recurs inside the span, and two such devices stand in the span's own bytes - one of them spliced by the row itself.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale ends by asserting that no new narrative-onset marker, a fresh time-frame or scene turn, recurs to divide the unit; no digit-bearing sweep citation accompanies it, and the universals checker flags exactly this clause (the only universals flag across the eight rows of this slice). The row's own byte-tier splice from oshb:Isa.20.2 opens בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא (byte tier), a verse-initial time frame that stands at only 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, oshb:Isa.18.7 and oshb:Isa.20.2). A second scene-turn device stands verse-internally at oshb:Isa.20.6: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ (byte tier), one of 45 verses carrying that onset book-wide (sweep: 45 verses, skeleton tier) - and one of the seven sites beyond its own span that the row covering Isa.19.16-Isa.19.25 counts when it makes that same device its structuring driver across chapters 19-24. The interior seam the row does argue against, at Isa.20.2|Isa.20.3 before the divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), is also exactly where the single-witness setumah the inventory records at Isa.20.2 falls. The whole-chapter reading remains defensible on content and the confidence already sits at the whole-chapter cap; the warrant as written does not survive its own bytes.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the undigited exclusivity clause with a digit-bearing formulation that names and disposes of both interior sites - the Isa.20.2 time frame and the Isa.20.6 scene turn. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The operative-category deviation is disclosed in strongest_rejected_alternative rather than device_notes, and in consequence that field carries a label rival instead of the byte-strongest span rival.
findings.grounds: unit_type is vision_report over a span narrated in the third person from start to finish; the operative-category law requires the one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes, and the neighbouring Isa.16.1-Isa.16.5 row places its own deviation disclosure there. Here strongest_rejected_alternative holds it instead, while device_notes carries only the mark record and the whole-chapter cap note. The span rival that field would otherwise weigh - an internal cut at Isa.20.2|Isa.20.3 opened by the divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), a ruled tier-1 frame signal, with the single-witness setumah recorded at Isa.20.2 falling exactly there - is argued only in passing inside the rationale.
findings.proposed_change: Move the operative-category deviation sentence to device_notes and give strongest_rejected_alternative the Isa.20.2|Isa.20.3 span rival. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: device_notes narrates campaign policy and review posture rather than the substrate.
findings.grounds: device_notes states that the confidence sits at the whole-chapter cap the campaign sets for that shape, not at a level implying any fresh evidentiary problem. The register purge bars workflow and administrative language from row prose in every field: the cap is process policy and the trailing clause is commentary on the review rather than on the text. The underlying application is correct - the span covers chapter 20 in full at six verses, and medium_low is the capped value.
findings.proposed_change: State the whole-chapter shape and its confidence without narrating the policy or the review posture. No span change proposed.
